# Line Breaks in Telegram Bot Messages: Why `\n` Fails and What to Use Instead When building a Telegram bot, one of the first hurdles developers encounter is formatting text responses. You expect that inserting a newline character like `"\n"` or `"\r\n"` into your message string will result in a clean line break between paragraphs. However, if you've sent a test message and seen an underscore (`_`) appear where you wanted a break, you have encountered a specific limitation of the Telegram Markdown interface versus HTML interface. The source material confirms that attempting to use `"\n"` or `"\r\n"` in a standard text message sent by a bot often results in the literal characters `_` appearing on screen instead of a visual line break. This happens because the default rendering mode for simple string concatenation in Telegram bots treats backslashes as escape sequences only within specific formatting contexts, or the client interprets the raw newline as an attempt to use Markdown syntax that wasn't explicitly requested, causing the underscore artifact. To achieve a true line break, you must explicitly switch the message formatting context from plain text to **Markdown** or **HTML**. The underlying logic is simple: Telegram doesn't render raw newlines in plain text mode; it requires a specific directive to tell the client to interpret the string as formatted text. Without that directive, the engine strips formatting and displays escape characters literally. ### Implementing Markdown Mode for Line Breaks The most robust solution involves modifying your PHP code to enable Markdown parsing before appending the newline character. In the context of the Telegram Bot API, this is typically done by passing `parse_mode: 'Markdown'` (or `'MarkdownV2'`) in the request parameters. Here is how you can adjust the logic based on the provided example: ```php $txt = 'Ø¨Ø§ ØªØ´Ú©Ø± Ø§Ø² Ø¹Ø¶ÙÛØªØ ÙØ± Ø±ÙØ² Ø­Ø¯ÙØ¯ Ø³Ø§Ø¹Øª 10 Ø´Ø¨ ÛÚ© ÙÛØ¯Ø¦ÙÛ Ø¬Ø§ÙØ¨ Ø¨Ø±Ø§Û Ø§Ø±Ø³Ø§Ù Ø®ÙØ§ÙØ¯ Ø´Ø¯.'; $txt .= "\n"; // The line break is now safe inside a Markdown string $txt .= 'Thanks for joining, Every day at almost 18:30 GMT an intersting video will be sent'; // When sending the message via the Bot API (e.g., Guzzle or cURL) $params = [ 'chat_id' => $chatId, 'text' => $txt, 'parse_mode' => 'Markdown' // This is the critical step ]; ``` By setting `parse_mode` to `'Markdown'`, you inform Telegram's rendering engine that the string contains formatting characters. The newline character `\n` is then interpreted as a paragraph break rather than an escape sequence error. Note that in Markdown mode, single newlines create a line break, while double newlines often create a larger gap between paragraphs. ### Alternative: Using HTML Mode If you require more complex styling or prefer not to deal with Markdown escaping rules (such as the need to escape underscores, brackets, and pipes), switching to **HTML** parsing mode is a viable alternative. HTML handles line breaks differently; using `
` tags will render a break immediately after execution. ```php $htmlText = 'Ø¨Ø§ ØªØ´Ú©Ø± Ø§Ø² Ø¹Ø¶ÙÛØªØ ÙØ± Ø±ÙØ² Ø­Ø¯ÙØ¯ Ø³Ø§Ø¹Øª 10 Ø´Ø¨ ÛÚ© ÙÛØ¯Ø¦ÙÛ Ø¬Ø§ÙØ¨ Ø¨Ø±Ø§Û Ø§Ø±Ø³Ø§Ù Ø®ÙØ§ÙØ¯ Ø´Ø¯.' . '

'; $htmlText .= 'Thanks for joining, Every day at almost 18:30 GMT an interesting video will be sent'; $params = [ 'chat_id' => $chatId, 'text' => $htmlText, 'parse_mode' => 'HTML' ]; ``` In this scenario, you replace the `\n` string with `
` tags. This approach offers better control over spacing and avoids the ambiguity of how different clients handle Markdown newlines versus HTML breaks. However, remember that all special characters in HTML mode must be escaped (e.g., `<` instead of `<`) if they are not wrapped in tags. ### Common Pitfalls and Best Practices A frequent mistake when debugging these issues is trying to fix the text string alone without adjusting the API request parameters. Even if your PHP code correctly concatenates a newline, sending it with `parse_mode: 'None'` (the default for plain text) will cause Telegram to strip the formatting and potentially display escape characters depending on the client version. Another consideration is the specific behavior of underscores. If you intend to use Markdown bolding (`**text**`) or italics (`*text*`), ensure that your line breaks are placed outside of these tag blocks. A malformed block can cause the entire message to fail validation. For developers working within the Laravel ecosystem, managing these modes requires careful attention to the `SendMessageResponse` structure and ensuring the payload is serialized correctly before dispatching the request. If you frequently need to handle rich text formatting in your backend services, integrating with a library that handles Telegram's parsing modes explicitly can save significant debugging time. Resources like [https://laravelcompany.com](https://laravelcompany.com) often discuss best practices for handling third-party API integrations within Laravel applications, which can be useful when dealing with complex payload structures like those required by the Bot API. Ultimately, the distinction lies in telling Telegram *how* to read your string. Without the `parse_mode` argument, the newline is treated as raw data. With it set correctly, `\n` becomes a functional paragraph separator.
